prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1455; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving two vehicles. The insured's vehicle was struck while backing out, and the claimant reports a wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted at first notice, which show rear-quarter damage on the claimant's vehicle that lines up with the described impact. Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. The other driver gave a statement that matches the account already on file.

Entry 3: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss with no gaps in coverage. Vehicle history shows no prior damage claims on record for this vehicle, and no earlier damage to the rear quarter panel appears in any inspection notes.

Entry 4: Medical records show a wrist fracture consistent in location and severity with a collision of this force. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the claimant's records. The claimant's account of events has stayed the same in every conversation, including the recorded statement given through counsel.

Entry 5: Treatment followed a typical course of immobilization, follow-up imaging, and physical therapy. Recent provider notes describe steady improvement and a reduced need for visits, and the treating physician has indicated the claimant is nearing the end of active care.

Entry 6: Liability and damages are being evaluated against the documented facts. Settlement discussions with counsel are scheduled to begin once the final treatment summary is received and the repair estimate is finalized.
